[ASSISTANT_SAID] One notable example is the recovery of the Aleutian Canada goose, which was once critically endangered with a population of fewer than 800 individuals in the 1970s.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Conservation efforts, including habitat restoration and predator control, have helped increase the Aleutian Canada goose population to over 70,000 individuals today.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Another success story is the removal of non-native foxes from some islands, which has helped protect native bird populations from predation.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Aleutian Islands population of sea otters was largely wiped out due to hunting and oil spills, but conservation efforts have helped the population rebound.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The western population of Steller's eiders, a diving duck, is also endangered and is actively managed through a conservation plan that includes monitoring, research, and habitat restoration.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Aleutian Islands are home to several species of whales, including the endangered western stock of gray whales, with ongoing efforts aimed at studying and protecting them.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Harsh and unpredictable weather conditions can make fieldwork challenging and dangerous.
